A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ELECTRA research work. All 30 pages, including equations, figures, tables, Appendices A-L and the checklist, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original ELECTRA evaluations on QM9 and six MD molecules, component ablations, Gaussian overfitting experiments and DFT initialization results.

after.justification: v5 retains those original benchmark, ablation, overfitting and DFT initialization results.

M1.justification: The Gaussian-mixture representation, HotPP backbone, symmetry-breaking initialization, debiasing layers, readout heads, density normalization and training objective are unchanged. The notation corrections do not alter the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use QM9 and the same six-molecule MD dataset. The DFT initialization, single-snapshot overfitting and molecular visualization scenarios are also retained without coverage changes.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same DeepDFT, GPWNO, InfGCN, ChargE3Net and SCDP variants; Table 2 retains SCDP, GPWNO and InfGCN. Atomic-superposition initialization remains the DFT baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains the QM9 split of 123,835 training, 50 validation and 10,000 test molecules, NMAE metric, full-grid evaluation and training budgets. Appendices H, I and K retain the same overfitting protocol, hyperparameters and DFT settings.

E4.justification: Appendix J retains all five component ablations, and Appendix H retains the Gaussian overfitting analysis testing basis limitations. Figures 1-4 and their symmetry, directional-bias and molecular-density analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates without error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. Checklist item 7 retains the computational-cost explanation; no seed or repeated-run information is added.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match, including ELECTRA's 0.176% QM9 NMAE and 0.089-second inference time in Table 1, MD and overfitting results in Table 2, ablations in Table 4, and the 50.72% average SCF-iteration reduction.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions and derivations retain their meaning. Correcting duplicated edge subscripts in Section 2.2 and removing a stray closing bracket from Equation 40 are typographical fixes without changes to mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same floating-orbital novelty, equivariance, accuracy-efficiency and DFT acceleration claims. Their scope and the concluding discussion are unchanged.

C2.justification: Both retain the qualifications concerning eigenvector canonicalization and degenerate inertia tensors, the need for adaptation to periodic systems, and the hybrid-orbital proposal. Appendix H's interpretation of model error versus basis limitations is unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, hyperparameters, hardware, training costs and VASP parameters are unchanged. Both PDFs provide the same code/data access information and MIT-license statement; Appendix K receives only a grammatical correction.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work positioning are identical. Bibliography entries move across page breaks following the expanded acknowledgements, without additions or removals.

P1.justification: v5 makes localized capitalization, grammar and notation corrections and slightly shortens one sentence. It also adds Jonas Elsborg as a corresponding author and acknowledges NitroScale funding. Section order and narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded acknowledgements reflow bibliography entries across pages 11-15, and the title-page correspondence text changes slightly. Figures 1-4 and Tables 1-5 retain their artwork, captions, structure and placement.

improvement.justification: v5 modestly improves editorial precision by correcting inconsistent edge subscripts in Section 2.2, the stray bracket in Equation 40 and several prose errors. These fixes improve presentation accuracy; the method, scientific arguments, empirical evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
